prompt: Review an unseen sanitized Cassandra, vector-search and metadata-catalog evidence packet. Defend the data models, correctness and freshness contracts, capacity, maintenance, security, recovery and cost; recover one reviewer-injected incident; then revise the design after a major topology, workload, model, filter, privacy, retention or RTO constraint changes.
deliverables: Consumer operations, SLIs, authorities and three complete request/state paths.
Cassandra query-to-key model, topology, consistency, timestamp, hot-partition and bounded-result defense.
Repair, tombstone, grace, compaction, headroom, backup and restore proof.
Exact or labeled recall/relevance by critical slice with latency and resource trade-offs.
Catalog source identity, checkpoint, ingestion, metadata-store and search freshness map.
Least privilege, sensitive metadata/vector/data copy lifecycle, audit and secrets boundary.
Incident timeline, reversible containment, calculations, changed-constraint defense and exact teardown.
evidenceRequirements: Reviewer provides unfamiliar synthetic operations, topology, metrics, repair/compaction/backup, vector evaluation/index/distribution, catalog ingestion/lineage/access and cost evidence.
No shared service, real credential, customer data, host network/clock mutation, unbounded repair/compaction/rebuild/load or unknown cleanup.
Claims join exact identities, versions and time; averages are not used as identity-specific proof.
Write timeout outcome and timestamp authority remain explicit.
Deletion safety uses observed range coverage and horizon arithmetic.
Vector quality compares against exact or reviewed labels by critical slice.
Vector capacity includes replicas, indexes and migration/rebuild overlap.
Catalog absence is not treated as no dependency without observation coverage.
Restore validates consumer correctness, semantic identity and RPO/RTO.
Reviewer observes incident recovery, changed-constraint revision, delayed explanation and cleanup.
